CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left lower back pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports left-sided lower back pain. He underwent lumbar microdiscectomy in November 2020 for disk herniation with compression of the spinal thecal sac. Prior to surgery, he experienced severe nerve pain radiating down his leg and back, which was managed with high-dose gabapentin; he notes it was difficult to discontinue this medication. Currently, his left lower back pain is generally localized to his previous surgical site, though pain location varies day to day and may involve the right side as well. Stretching provides relief. Bending over exacerbates pain, and he reports pain occurring randomly. He has not attempted icing. He is taking ibuprofen 800 mg daily. He denies current leg pain and nerve pain.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies leg pain, nerve pain, or other problems.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Lumbar microdiscectomy November 2020

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen 800 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Back examination performed. Forward flexion without pain. Extension without pain. Pain with weightbearing/standing. Pain with palpation on the left side at L5 level. No pain with right-sided palpation. Dorsiflexion normal. Range of motion normal. Lower extremities without pain or evidence of nerve pain.

RESULTS
X-ray of the spine: No fractures. Surgical site appears to have healed appropriately.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Muscle pull with spinal misalignment. Physical therapy referral. Meloxicam prescribed in place of ibuprofen. Referral to pain management clinic for discussion of pain management strategies and non-narcotic options. Demerol prescribed.
